title: Revisiting Third-Party Library Detection: A Ground Truth Dataset and Its Implications Across Security Tasks
objective: Construct realistic version-level Android TPL ground truth and reevaluate state-of-the-art detectors under a shared benchmark.
inputs_and_assumptions: Real Android applications with remote and local dependency evidence; tool-specific reference profiling and compatibility constraints remain relevant.
ground_truth_and_dataset: The benchmark contains more than 6,000 applications with version-level annotations. The standardized detector comparison uses a 946-application compatible slice and preserves the benchmark's stated limitations as a practical approximation rather than an absolute standard.
transformation_findings: R8-era shrinking and optimization expose substantial recall and version-discrimination weaknesses; results depend on method family and compatibility.
uncertainty_and_limitations: Ground truth is described by the authors as a practical approximation.
Only compatible tools and applications can enter the common evaluation slice.
Cross-tool results diagnose limitations but do not provide a new production detector.
artifact_availability: The paper presents TPL-Benchmark and TPL-Extractor as open research artifacts.
sbom_relevance: Directly supports realistic evaluation, denominator transparency, identity/version separation, and caution against treating original-paper metrics as universal.
